page.overview:
What is Bar-en-Danwedh?

Amon Rûdh, also known as Bald Hill, was a hill south of Brethil in West Beleriand.

The hill was made of stone and rose about a thousand feet high. It lay at the southeastern end of the Moors of the Nibin-noeg. Thickets of Aeglos grew on its lower slopes, but only deep red flowers called Seregon grew on its top, making it seem blood-covered.

Mîm the Petty-dwarf lived within Amon Rûdh with his two sons, Ibûn and Khîm. They referred to the hill as Sharbhund in their own tongue. Mîm was captured by a group of outlaws led by Túrin Turambar and forced to reveal the location of his refuge, known as Bar-en-Nibin-Noeg (House of the Petty-Dwarves). When it was discovered that Khîm, who had been shot by a member of Túrin's band, was mortally wounded and later died of his wounds, Túrin repented and offered his services to Mîm, promising to provide a ransom to atone for Khîm's death. From then on, Mîm tolerated the presence of the outlaws, promising to house Túrin's band in exchange for his life. The dwelling was then called Bar-en-Danwedh (House of Ransom).

Amon Rûdh became the base of operations for the outlaws, and with the arrival of Beleg, it became the heart of the area known as Dor-Cúarthol "Land of Bow and Helm" (referring to the Two Captains, Beleg and Túrin). It served as a center of resistance against the forces of Morgoth. Túrin's location was eventually discovered, and the outlaws were slain by the Orcs, covering the hilltop with blood.
